item.title: 1.1 Why Spiking Neural Networks Exist
item.description: Imagine a small sensor watching a quiet room. For long stretches, the scene barely changes.

item.title: 1. Why Spiking Neural Networks Matters
item.description: 1. Why Spiking Neural Networks Matters This teaching step is conceptually distinct and could not be merged without blurring two different ideas.

item.title: 2.1 Neurons, Synapses, and Membrane Potential
item.description: Neurons, Synapses, and Membrane Potential A spike becomes useful only when one neuron can receive it, respond to it, and pass a new spike onward.

item.title: 2.2 Action Potentials, Refractory Dynamics, and Spike Trains
item.description: Action Potentials, Refractory Dynamics, and Spike Trains A neuron’s membrane potential changes as charged ions move across its membrane through voltage-gated ion channels.

item.title: 2.3 Constraint Geometry in Spiking Networks
item.description: Constraint Geometry in Spiking Networks A leaky integrate-and-fire neuron already gives us a useful picture of controlled accumulation: synaptic input changes a membrane voltage, leakage pulls that voltage downward, and reaching a threshold triggers a spike.

item.title: 2.4 Why Spike Derivatives Need Surrogates
item.description: Why Spike Derivatives Need Surrogates Backpropagation through time has already given us a way to trace how activity at many time steps contributes to a final error.

item.title: 2.5 How Sparse Events Can Save Energy
item.description: How Sparse Events Can Save Energy A neuron receives signals through synapses, combines their effects in its membrane state, and emits a spike when that state reaches the firing condition.
